title: Correlation Flow Sparkline: lightweight session drilldown
creator: Ana Velasquez
description: Introduce a compact, horizontally-scrolling Correlation Flow Sparkline component for the Redwood Console request drilldown. This component surfaces span-level timing, key correlation IDs, and hit/miss flags for cached KV prefixes in a dense row above the main timeline so engineers can scan sessions quickly. We expect this to improve mean time to resolution for tail-latency investigations by making causal chains and cache effects visible at a glance without opening full span detail panes.
acceptance_criteria: Sparkline row renders for requests with >=1 child spans and aligns with timeline timebase
Hovering a sparkline segment highlights the corresponding span in the main waterfall and shows a compact tooltip with span name, duration, correlation IDs, and KV cache flag
Clicking a correlation badge filters the request list to related correlation ID across the current query window
Sparkline integrates with existing timeline zoom and pan; segments reflow correctly when time range changes
Performance: sparkline render for a page of 50 sessions should not exceed 120ms initial paint on typical dev laptop
design_decisions: Use a single-row sparkline per session to preserve vertical density in lists; expand to multi-row only in expanded session view
Encode correlation ID hits as colored micro-badges (teal) and cache-misses as outlined badges to preserve color budget for status overlays
Tooltips are lightweight HTML overlays (not portal-heavy) to avoid DOM churn; full-span detail still available via existing inspector panel
Adopt existing console color tokens and micro-typography to maintain parity with dashboard lists
Defer embedding log lines into the sparkline tooltip; link out to logs panel to avoid coupling and large payload fetches
